comment: RS (Edexcel IGCSE 4RS1, Christianity) multiple choice — Paper 2 The Religious Community, Sections 1-3 (modules 05-07). Key terms, scripture and quotations, and who said what. Built from the school's lesson slides, the Section 1-3 revision booklets, the Religious Community 1 model answers and the specification. Four options; answer is the 0-based index of the correct one.

05-origins-and-their-impact.q: How many books does the Bible contain?
05-origins-and-their-impact.explain: 66 — the Old Testament (the Jewish scriptures) and the New Testament (the Christian scriptures).

05-origins-and-their-impact.q: Which book of the New Testament is a history of the early church, written by St Luke?
05-origins-and-their-impact.explain: Acts. The other New Testament types are the four Gospels, the letters (mostly Paul's) and the apocalypse, Revelation.

05-origins-and-their-impact.q: "All scripture is inspired by God and profitable for teaching, for reproof, for correction, and for training in righteousness" comes from…
05-origins-and-their-impact.explain: 2 Timothy 3:16-17. It is the standard proof text for the Bible's authority — fundamentalists stress "inspired by God", others stress "profitable for teaching".

05-origins-and-their-impact.q: Which view holds that the Bible is the verbally inspired word of God, literally true and without error?
05-origins-and-their-impact.explain: The fundamentalist view, generally held by evangelical Protestants. It grew up in nineteenth-century America to defend Christianity against science and modernism.

05-origins-and-their-impact.q: On the conservative view of the Bible, Genesis 1 explains…
options: why the world was created, but not necessarily how
exactly how the world was created, in six days
a Babylonian creation story borrowed by the Jews
05-origins-and-their-impact.explain: Conservatives — probably most Christians — hold the Bible to be inspired rather than dictated, so Genesis 1 gives the purpose of creation rather than a scientific account.

05-origins-and-their-impact.q: On the liberal view of the Bible, Genesis 1 is…
options: the direct dictation of the Holy Spirit
a forgery added in the Middle Ages
05-origins-and-their-impact.explain: Liberals hold that Genesis 1 is largely symbolic and that scientific explanations of origins are preferable; the Bible contains God's word but was written with the mindset of its time.

05-origins-and-their-impact.q: The three sources of authority held in creative tension by the Church of England are…
options: Scripture, Natural Law and the Magisterium
05-origins-and-their-impact.explain: Scripture, Tradition and Reason. The Church of England rejects the authority of the Pope and the primacy of Natural Law over Scripture.

05-origins-and-their-impact.q: Who is the Supreme Governor of the Church of England?
05-origins-and-their-impact.explain: The monarch. The Archbishop of Canterbury is the most senior bishop, Primate of All England; the Archbishop of York is second.

05-origins-and-their-impact.q: Who said "Reason increases and enlarges human understanding of divine revelation"?
05-origins-and-their-impact.explain: Michael Ramsey, a former Archbishop of Canterbury. It is the standard citation for Reason as an Anglican source of authority.

05-origins-and-their-impact.q: Who said "He who acts against his conscience sins"?
05-origins-and-their-impact.explain: Aquinas. He treated the conscience as a rational person's natural ability to tell right from wrong, and Catholic teaching holds that a conscience must always be obeyed.

05-origins-and-their-impact.q: Which New Testament writer speaks of "what the law requires" being "written on their hearts"?
05-origins-and-their-impact.explain: St Paul, in Romans 2:15-16. It is the strongest biblical support for treating the conscience as the inner voice of God.

05-origins-and-their-impact.q: Who argued that the conscience is a controlling influence over a person's passions, balancing self-love with benevolence towards others?
05-origins-and-their-impact.explain: Joseph Butler. He divided a person into passions, appetites and affections on one side, and benevolence, self-love and conscience on the other.

05-origins-and-their-impact.q: In Freud's model of the mind, which part is formed in infancy out of the morals learnt from one's parents?
05-origins-and-their-impact.explain: The super-ego — the restraining, censoring part. Freud's account makes the conscience a product of socialisation rather than of God, and it can be so severe that it produces guilt and acute self-criticism.

05-origins-and-their-impact.q: Who called the conscience "the voice of man pretending to be the voice of God"?
05-origins-and-their-impact.explain: Bonhoeffer. He held that original sin broke the connection between God and humanity, so treating the conscience as God's voice is idolatry; the example of Christ is the better moral guide.

05-origins-and-their-impact.q: Apostolic succession links a Roman Catholic bishop back to…
05-origins-and-their-impact.explain: St Peter. The laying on of hands at ordination is believed to carry the line unbroken, and the Pope, as Bishop of Rome, has inherited St Peter's authority.

05-origins-and-their-impact.q: Who argued for a "priesthood of all believers"?
05-origins-and-their-impact.explain: Martin Luther — that the clergy have no unique powers and all Christians can be channels of God's word. It is why Protestants give the laity a far larger role.

05-origins-and-their-impact.q: What is ordination?
options: The election of a bishop by a diocese
A promise of celibacy made by a priest
The ceremony by which a church appoints its ministers
The consecration of bread and wine
05-origins-and-their-impact.explain: The ceremony appointing a church's ministers, in which the Holy Spirit is believed to pass to the ordinand by the laying on of hands. It is a sacrament for Roman Catholics; Protestant groups do not regard the ceremony as important.

05-origins-and-their-impact.q: In which village was Jesus raised?
05-origins-and-their-impact.explain: Nazareth, in Galilee. He was born in Bethlehem in Judea; almost nothing of his childhood is recorded between the birth and the baptism.

05-origins-and-their-impact.q: Which Roman historian records that Christians were named after "Christus", who suffered the extreme penalty under Pontius Pilate?
05-origins-and-their-impact.explain: Tacitus. Josephus, the Jewish historian, is the other non-Christian source: "about this time there lived Jesus, a wise man".

05-origins-and-their-impact.q: At Jesus' baptism, the Spirit of God descended in the form of…
05-origins-and-their-impact.explain: A dove. Three things happened: the heavens opened, the Spirit descended as a dove, and a voice from heaven spoke.

05-origins-and-their-impact.q: "You are my beloved son with whom I am well pleased" was spoken at…
05-origins-and-their-impact.explain: Jesus' baptism in the Jordan by John the Baptist. It gives Jesus the Father's blessing and is used to argue the baptism is his commissioning and proof that he is the Son of God.

05-origins-and-their-impact.q: How long did Jesus spend fasting in the wilderness before the temptations?
05-origins-and-their-impact.explain: Forty days and nights — which is why Lent lasts forty days and why Christians reflect on the temptations during it.

05-origins-and-their-impact.q: Which of these was NOT one of the three temptations of Jesus?
options: To throw himself from the highest point of the temple
To worship the devil in return for all the kingdoms of the world
05-origins-and-their-impact.explain: Turning water into wine is the miracle at Cana, not a temptation. The three temptations were material need, spectacle, and power.

05-origins-and-their-impact.q: Jesus healed the leper by touching him. Why does that detail matter?
options: It proved the disease was not contagious
Lepers were unclean outcasts under the Law, so it showed Jesus' authority was greater than the Law
It showed Jesus needed physical contact to heal
It fulfilled a prophecy of Zechariah
05-origins-and-their-impact.explain: Under Jewish law lepers were unclean and lived on the margins. The Law could only label a person clean; Jesus makes them clean — so he is greater than the Law.

05-origins-and-their-impact.q: In the exorcism of Legion, Jesus sent the demons into…
05-origins-and-their-impact.explain: A herd of pigs, which stampeded down the bank into the sea and drowned. It happened in the gentile country of the Gerasenes, showing Jesus' mission is for Jew and gentile alike.

05-origins-and-their-impact.q: "My house shall be called a house of prayer, but you make it a den of robbers" was said when Jesus…
05-origins-and-their-impact.explain: At the cleansing of the Temple, when he overturned the money-changers' tables. It is the immediate reason the high priests plotted to kill him.

05-origins-and-their-impact.q: At the Last Supper Jesus took the wine and said…
options: "this is my blood of the covenant which is poured out for many"
05-origins-and-their-impact.explain: It presents his death as a sacrifice and as a new covenant, and it is the foundation of Holy Communion.

05-origins-and-their-impact.q: Jesus' words on the cross, "My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?", are used by Christians to show…
options: that Jesus had lost his faith
the genuine humanity of Jesus in his suffering
that God had abandoned the world
that the crucifixion was a mistake
05-origins-and-their-impact.explain: They show a fully human Jesus in real anguish. The same scene adds the darkened sky, the temple veil split in two, and the centurion's verdict.

05-origins-and-their-impact.q: Who said "Truly this man was the Son of God" at the crucifixion?
05-origins-and-their-impact.explain: A Roman centurion — a gentile. Christians use it to argue that Jesus came for gentiles as well as Jews.

05-origins-and-their-impact.q: "It is costly because it costs a man his life, and it is grace because it gives a man the only true life" describes…
05-origins-and-their-impact.explain: Bonhoeffer on costly grace, in The Cost of Discipleship (1937). He contrasted it with cheap grace — thinking you are saved without having to do anything.

06-celebration-and-pilgrimage.q: The word "Advent" comes from a word meaning…
06-celebration-and-pilgrimage.explain: From the Latin adventum. The season looks forward both to Christmas and to Jesus' promised return as judge and king.

06-celebration-and-pilgrimage.q: When does Advent begin?
options: On the fourth Sunday before Christmas
On the first Sunday of December
06-celebration-and-pilgrimage.explain: The fourth Sunday before Christmas; it ends on Christmas Eve.

06-celebration-and-pilgrimage.q: How many candles are there on an Advent crown?
06-celebration-and-pilgrimage.explain: Four — one lit on each Sunday of Advent, so the light grows as the wait shortens, pointing to Jesus as the light of the world.

06-celebration-and-pilgrimage.q: At a Christingle service, what does the orange represent?
06-celebration-and-pilgrimage.explain: The orange is the world and the lit candle is Jesus, the light of the world, sent to save it from sin.

06-celebration-and-pilgrimage.q: At a Christingle service, what does the red ribbon represent?
06-celebration-and-pilgrimage.explain: The red ribbon signifies his suffering; the fruit or sweets on the cocktail sticks are the fruits of the natural world provided by God.

06-celebration-and-pilgrimage.q: On what date do Orthodox Christians celebrate Christmas?
06-celebration-and-pilgrimage.explain: 7 January, because they use the Julian calendar — twelve days after the Western date.

06-celebration-and-pilgrimage.q: Who decided on 25 December as the date of Christmas?
06-celebration-and-pilgrimage.explain: Pope Julius I, in the fourth century, as an attempt to Christianise the Pagan celebrations already held then. By 529 AD it was a civil holiday.

06-celebration-and-pilgrimage.q: Which Roman festival was already being celebrated in late December?
06-celebration-and-pilgrimage.explain: Saturnalia, held in the second half of December. The Gospels give no date for Jesus' birth.

06-celebration-and-pilgrimage.q: Christmas celebrates the incarnation, which means…
options: the coming of the Holy Spirit
06-celebration-and-pilgrimage.explain: God becoming human in Jesus. Its importance is two-fold: as a man Jesus showed how people should behave, and as God he revealed God's own nature.

06-celebration-and-pilgrimage.q: Twelve days after Christmas, at Epiphany, what changes at the church crib?
options: The shepherds are removed and the wise men put in their place
The infant Jesus is placed in the manger
06-celebration-and-pilgrimage.explain: The infant is placed in the manger on Christmas Eve; at Epiphany the wise men replace the shepherds.

06-celebration-and-pilgrimage.q: Who banned the celebration of Christmas in the 1640s for encouraging "liberty to carnal and sensual delights"?
06-celebration-and-pilgrimage.explain: Oliver Cromwell — even Christmas puddings were banned. It is useful evidence that complaints about Christmas losing its religious meaning are not new.

06-celebration-and-pilgrimage.q: The name "Shrove Tuesday" comes from a word meaning…
06-celebration-and-pilgrimage.explain: From "shriven", meaning forgiven: Christians attended church that day to confess their sins before Lent began, and ate up the forbidden foods.

06-celebration-and-pilgrimage.q: The ashes used on Ash Wednesday come from…
options: incense burnt at the Easter Vigil
06-celebration-and-pilgrimage.explain: Last year's Palm Sunday crosses are collected and burnt. The ash marks a cross on the forehead as a sign of humility and of a focus on spiritual rather than worldly concerns.

06-celebration-and-pilgrimage.q: How long is Lent?
06-celebration-and-pilgrimage.explain: Forty days of fasting and penitence, recalling Jesus' forty days in the wilderness. Catholics typically give up a luxury; Orthodox Christians refrain from meat and dairy.

06-celebration-and-pilgrimage.q: "Hosanna to the Son of David! Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord! Hosanna in the highest!" is remembered on…
06-celebration-and-pilgrimage.explain: Palm Sunday (Matthew 21:9), Jesus' triumphal entry into Jerusalem. Worshippers are given blessed palm crosses.

06-celebration-and-pilgrimage.q: Which day of Holy Week remembers Jesus washing his disciples' feet and instituting the Eucharist?
06-celebration-and-pilgrimage.explain: Maundy Thursday. The priest may wash the feet of twelve of the congregation; traditionally the Pope washes twelve people's feet and the British monarch gives out Maundy Money.

06-celebration-and-pilgrimage.q: Why are altars and churches stripped of decorations on Good Friday?
options: To make room for the Easter garden
Because decoration is forbidden during Lent
To remind Christians of Jesus' abandonment and remove distractions from worship
Because the church is cleaned before Easter
06-celebration-and-pilgrimage.explain: It recalls Jesus' abandonment and leaves nothing to distract from reflection on his death. Some Christians attend a three-hour service from noon to 3pm, or a procession of witness carrying a cross.

06-celebration-and-pilgrimage.q: The Greek letters alpha and omega on the paschal candle show that Christ is…
06-celebration-and-pilgrimage.explain: The beginning and the end. The candle also bears a cross for the crucifixion and five pieces of incense for the five wounds of Christ.

06-celebration-and-pilgrimage.q: The five pieces of incense set into the paschal candle represent…
options: the five loaves of the feeding of the five thousand
the five days of Holy Week
06-celebration-and-pilgrimage.explain: The five wounds of Christ. The candle is lit from a fire outside the church at the Easter Vigil and carried in as the priest announces three times that Christ is risen.

06-celebration-and-pilgrimage.q: In a church's Easter garden, what happens on Easter Sunday?
options: Flowers are planted around the tomb
The stone is rolled back to show the grave is empty
A paschal candle is set inside the tomb
A flat stone is placed across the entrance
06-celebration-and-pilgrimage.explain: The stone is placed across the entrance on Easter Saturday to recall the burial, and rolled back on Easter Sunday to show the resurrection.

06-celebration-and-pilgrimage.q: Which passage argues that if Christ has not been raised, "our proclamation has been in vain and your faith has been in vain"?
06-celebration-and-pilgrimage.explain: 1 Corinthians 15, St Paul. It is the strongest argument that Easter is the most important Christian festival.

06-celebration-and-pilgrimage.q: A pilgrimage is best defined as…
options: a sacred journey undertaken for spiritual reasons
a journey every Christian is obliged to make once
a visit to the burial place of a saint
a holiday taken during a religious festival
06-celebration-and-pilgrimage.explain: A sacred journey in which God is encountered through the places, people and situations met. It is not an obligation in Christianity, and the physical journey mirrors an inner one.

06-celebration-and-pilgrimage.q: Who wrote "All pilgrimages should be stopped. There is no good in them: no commandment enjoins them, no obedience attaches to them"?
06-celebration-and-pilgrimage.explain: Martin Luther, in The Christian Nobility (1520). The Protestant Reformers feared that venerating relics broke the second commandment against idols.

06-celebration-and-pilgrimage.q: Pilgrims enter the Church of the Nativity in Bethlehem through a very low door known as…
06-celebration-and-pilgrimage.explain: The door of humility. It was originally built to stop thieves plundering the church, but it makes every pilgrim bow to the Christ child.

06-celebration-and-pilgrimage.q: What marks the spot in Bethlehem where Jesus is believed to have been born?
06-celebration-and-pilgrimage.explain: A fourteen-pointed star in the Grotto of the Nativity. Nearby is the Chapel of the Manger, where Mary is believed to have laid him.

06-celebration-and-pilgrimage.q: Tradition holds that the Milk Grotto near Bethlehem is where…
options: the shepherds were visited by the angel
Mary was told she would bear a son
the Holy Family sheltered during the Slaughter of the Innocents
the magi rested on their journey
06-celebration-and-pilgrimage.explain: The Holy Family sheltered there before the flight into Egypt, and a drop of Mary's milk is said to have turned the ground white. Both Christians and Muslims believe scrapings from the stones aid fertility.

06-celebration-and-pilgrimage.q: The church at Shepherds' Fields near Bethlehem is designed to look like…
06-celebration-and-pilgrimage.explain: A shepherd's tent. The site is where the angel told the shepherds to go to Bethlehem, and the church is dedicated to that angel.

06-celebration-and-pilgrimage.q: The Via Dolorosa in Jerusalem is…
options: the hill on which Jesus was crucified
the route Jesus is believed to have carried his cross
the garden where Jesus was arrested
the room of the Last Supper
06-celebration-and-pilgrimage.explain: The route from the outskirts of Jerusalem to the Church of the Holy Sepulchre. A procession each Friday says prayers at the Stations of the Cross, and many pilgrims walk it on Good Friday.

06-celebration-and-pilgrimage.q: Who had the visions of the Virgin Mary at Lourdes in 1858?
06-celebration-and-pilgrimage.explain: Bernadette Soubirous, a fourteen-year-old girl. She was told to drink at the spring beneath Mary's feet and to build a chapel there, and the link with healing was established when a sick baby given the water recovered.

06-celebration-and-pilgrimage.q: Taizé was founded in 1940 by Brother Roger as a community dedicated to…
06-celebration-and-pilgrimage.explain: Reconciliation. About a hundred Roman Catholic and Protestant monks belong to the ecumenical order, and tens of thousands of young people visit each year for the chant-based worship, Bible study and shared life.

07-worship-and-practice.q: A cruciform church is one that is…
07-worship-and-practice.explain: Cross-shaped. It is the traditional Anglican ground plan; a Baptist church is often just a square building.

07-worship-and-practice.q: The nave of a church is…
options: the part where the congregation sits
07-worship-and-practice.explain: The nave holds the congregation; the chancel is the part around the altar. A Baptist chapel is usually one undivided room.

07-worship-and-practice.q: What is the focal point of an Anglican church?
07-worship-and-practice.explain: The high altar, where the Eucharist is celebrated, decorated with cloth and candles — because Anglican worship centres on the Eucharist.

07-worship-and-practice.q: What is centre stage in a Baptist church?
07-worship-and-practice.explain: The pulpit, because Baptist worship centres on the preaching of the word. The Communion table is a simple wooden table that is not even central.

07-worship-and-practice.q: An Anglican lectern is often shaped like an eagle, symbolising…
07-worship-and-practice.explain: The spreading of the word. The lectern is where the Bible is read; the pulpit is where the sermon is preached.

07-worship-and-practice.q: An Anglican church has a font and a Baptist church a pool. Why?
options: Baptist churches have no running water
Anglicans baptise infants; Baptists immerse adults totally
07-worship-and-practice.explain: The furniture follows the theology. Baptists hold that only an adult can make their own choice, and that Jesus himself was baptised as an adult.

07-worship-and-practice.q: "For where two or three gather in my name, there am I with them" comes from…
07-worship-and-practice.explain: Matthew 18:20. It is the standard argument that Christians should worship together rather than alone.

07-worship-and-practice.q: Why do Christians gather for worship on Sunday?
options: It is the day of Jesus' resurrection
It is the day the Holy Spirit came
07-worship-and-practice.explain: Sunday is the day of the resurrection, so the timing of worship is itself a statement of belief.

07-worship-and-practice.q: A liturgy is…
options: a set order of service that is followed each time
a sermon based on the week's reading
the robes worn by a priest
07-worship-and-practice.explain: Catholic and Anglican worship is formal and liturgical; Baptist worship is informal and often follows no liturgy at all.

07-worship-and-practice.q: Transubstantiation is the belief that…
options: Christ is spiritually present in the bread and wine
the bread and wine really become Jesus' body and blood
the Eucharist is only a memorial of the Last Supper
the bread and wine must be consumed by the priest alone
07-worship-and-practice.explain: Held by Roman Catholics and Catholic Anglicans. Consubstantiation is the belief that Christ is spiritually present; the memorial view holds that nothing special happens.

07-worship-and-practice.q: Which belief holds that the Eucharist is just a memorial or re-creation of the Last Supper, with nothing special happening to the bread and wine?
07-worship-and-practice.explain: The memorial view, held by most Protestants. It fits their belief that Jesus' death was a "once for all" sacrifice that cannot be repeated.

07-worship-and-practice.q: Which two groups reject the Eucharist altogether?
07-worship-and-practice.explain: Quakers and the Salvation Army. Their practice is the strongest argument against "all Christians should celebrate the Eucharist".

07-worship-and-practice.q: Which command of Jesus does the Eucharist fulfil?
options: "Take up your cross and follow me"
07-worship-and-practice.explain: It makes the Eucharist an act of obedience rather than a preference, and it is the strongest argument that all Christians should celebrate it.

07-worship-and-practice.q: "Though we are many we are one body for we all partake of the one bread" is used to show that the Eucharist…
options: must be celebrated by a priest
replaces the sacrifice of the cross
07-worship-and-practice.explain: It is the sacrament of unity, which is why it cannot be a sign of fellowship if performed in isolation. It is also a sign of the new covenant.

07-worship-and-practice.q: Which type of prayer involves asking God for something, for oneself or for others?
07-worship-and-practice.explain: Supplication. The other three — adoration (praise), confession (repentance) and thanksgiving — make no request at all.

07-worship-and-practice.q: Which type of prayer is simply praising God?
07-worship-and-practice.explain: Adoration. Confession is saying sorry and repenting, and is a key part of all religious services.

07-worship-and-practice.q: Prayer has been described as "spiritual breathing" because it…
options: is something done constantly rather than occasionally
07-worship-and-practice.explain: It builds a relationship with God, communicates with him, gives hope and strength, and is how a Christian comes to understand God's will.

07-worship-and-practice.q: Who argued that a God who answers prayers while ignoring the Holocaust is not worth believing in?
07-worship-and-practice.explain: Maurice Wiles. It attacks God's character rather than his existence, which makes it stronger than ordinary complaints about unanswered prayer.

07-worship-and-practice.q: On a rosary, what is said on each of the five sets of ten small beads?
07-worship-and-practice.explain: A Hail Mary on each small bead; the four larger beads represent mysteries of the Passion and require the Lord's Prayer. It is a Catholic devotion and a form of meditation.

07-worship-and-practice.q: Meditating on an icon has been called "contemplation in colour". Which Christians chiefly do it?
07-worship-and-practice.explain: Orthodox Christians meditate on an image of Jesus or a saint as an encounter with God.

07-worship-and-practice.q: "Oh Lord Jesus Son of God, have mercy on me, a sinner" is…
07-worship-and-practice.explain: The Jesus Prayer, recited over and over, sometimes while walking or prostrating. It is a discipline focused on humility and detachment from the world.

07-worship-and-practice.q: Chrism is…
options: the blessed water of the font
the white robe worn at believers' baptism
the special oil a priest anoints a baptised child with
07-worship-and-practice.explain: The oil used to anoint the child. A candle is also often given, symbolising Jesus as light of the world and the move from darkness into light.

07-worship-and-practice.q: At an Anglican infant baptism, who makes the vows?
options: The godparents, on the child's behalf
07-worship-and-practice.explain: The godparents reject the devil and all rebellion against God, renounce the deceit and corruption of evil, repent of sin and turn to Christ as Saviour — because the infant cannot promise for itself.

07-worship-and-practice.q: At a believers' baptism, what does the candidate usually do before being baptised?
options: Receive the sign of the cross on the forehead
Make a testimony explaining their faith
07-worship-and-practice.explain: A testimony explaining their faith and their reasons for coming forward. They wear white, symbolising purity and the dress of an initiate.

07-worship-and-practice.q: At a believers' baptism the candidate is…
options: sprinkled with blessed water at the font
07-worship-and-practice.explain: Total immersion, usually in a pool and sometimes a river, in the name of the Father, Son and Holy Spirit. The immersion represents death, and the adult is thought to be born again.

07-worship-and-practice.q: "In baptism, God calls us out of darkness into his marvellous light. To follow Christ means dying to sin and rising to new life with him" comes from…
07-worship-and-practice.explain: The Anglican baptism service. It shows baptism is a death and resurrection in miniature, not a naming ceremony.

07-worship-and-practice.q: Which of these is a reason Christians give for the importance of baptism?
options: It guarantees a church wedding later
It admits a person to the priesthood
It replaces the need for confession
07-worship-and-practice.explain: Baptism is a sacrament and an initiation ritual, believed to wash away original sin, and it follows Jesus' own example of being baptised by John in the Jordan.

07-worship-and-practice.q: In the marriage service the priest joins the couple's hands and proclaims…
options: "Those whom God has called, let them answer"
"Love one another as I have loved you"
"What God has joined together let no one separate"
07-worship-and-practice.explain: Christians hold that God himself joins the couple and then helps sustain their relationship. Marriage is also held to be sanctioned by God — Jesus attended the wedding at Cana.

07-worship-and-practice.q: "I am the resurrection and the life. He who believes in me will live, even though he dies" is read as the coffin is brought into church. Where does it come from?
07-worship-and-practice.explain: John 11:25, at the Gathering. The service opens by denying that death is the end.

07-worship-and-practice.q: At the committal, the body is committed to the ground "earth to earth, ashes to ashes, dust to dust" — in what?
options: the sure and certain hope of the resurrection to eternal life
the peace of God which passes all understanding
the hope of forgiveness of sins
the name of the Father, Son and Holy Spirit
07-worship-and-practice.explain: The wording is the clearest evidence of what a funeral reveals about Christian beliefs about death: salvation for believers, God's mercy and strength, and the hope of resurrection.
